## 0. Setup

Load the package.

```{r}
# Load ggplot2 (run install.packages("ggplot2") once if it is missing)
install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)
```

Prepare the data.

```{r}
# Load the built-in mtcars dataset
data(mtcars)

# Turn cylinders into a factor so it is treated as a category
mtcars$cyl_f <- factor(mtcars$cyl)

# Copy the car names (row names) into a column so we can label points
mtcars$car <- rownames(mtcars)
```

## 1. geom_bar()

```{r}
# Start a plot with cylinder category on the x-axis
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl_f)) +
  # Draw bars whose height is the number of cars in each category
  geom_bar() +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_bar: cars per cylinder", x = "Cylinders", y = "Count")
```

**Result:** 3 bars: 4 cylinders = 11 cars, 6 cylinders = 7 cars, 8 cylinders = 14 cars.

## 2. geom_boxplot()

```{r}
# Start a plot with cylinders on x and mpg on y
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl_f, y = mpg)) +
  # Draw one boxplot per cylinder group (median, quartiles, outliers)
  geom_boxplot() +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_boxplot: mpg by cylinders", x = "Cylinders", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** mpg drops as cylinders increase (median about 26 for 4, 19.7 for 6, 15.2 for 8).

## 3. geom_density()

```{r}
# Start a plot using only mpg on the x-axis
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  # Draw a smooth curve showing how mpg values are distributed
  geom_density() +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_density: distribution of mpg", x = "mpg", y = "Density")
```

**Result:** a smooth curve with its peak around 15 to 20 mpg and a longer tail to the right.

## 4. geom_histogram()

```{r}
# Start a plot using only mpg on the x-axis
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  # Draw bars that count how many cars fall in each mpg bin (10 bins)
  geom_histogram(bins = 10) +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_histogram: distribution of mpg", x = "mpg", y = "Count")
```

**Result:** most cars fall between about 15 and 22 mpg, with fewer very efficient cars.

## 5. geom_hline()

```{r}
# Start a plot with weight on x and mpg on y
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  # Draw a horizontal line at the average mpg
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(mtcars$mpg), color = "red") +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_hline: average mpg", x = "Weight", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** one red horizontal line at y = 20.09 (the mean mpg). It is the only layer here, so there are no points.

## 6. geom_jitter()

```{r}
# Start a plot with cylinders on x and mpg on y
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl_f, y = mpg)) +
  # Draw each car as a point, shifted randomly sideways so points don't overlap
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2) +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_jitter: mpg by cylinders", x = "Cylinders", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** 32 points spread in 3 columns. Their positions shift slightly each time you run it because the jitter is random.

## 7. geom_line()

```{r}
# Start a plot with weight on x and mpg on y
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  # Connect the observations with a line, ordered by weight
  geom_line() +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_line: mpg vs weight", x = "Weight", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** a zigzag line that trends downward, meaning heavier cars have lower mpg.

## 8. geom_rug()

```{r}
# Start a plot with weight on x and mpg on y
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  # Draw small tick marks on both axes at every observed value
  geom_rug() +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_rug: where the data lies", x = "Weight", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** tick marks along the bottom and left edges, denser where more cars have similar values.

## 9. geom_text()

```{r}
# Start a plot with weight on x, mpg on y, and car names as labels
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, label = car)) +
  # Write each car's name at its position (small font so labels fit)
  geom_text(size = 3) +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_text: car names", x = "Weight", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** each car's name appears at its (weight, mpg) position, so you can see which car is which.

## 10. geom_violin()

```{r}
# Start a plot with cylinders on x and mpg on y
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl_f, y = mpg)) +
  # Draw a mirrored density shape for each group
  geom_violin() +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_violin: mpg by cylinders", x = "Cylinders", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** 3 violin shapes. The 4-cylinder one is highest and widest, and the 8-cylinder one sits lowest.

## 11. geom_vline()

```{r}
# Start a plot with weight on x and mpg on y
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  # Draw a vertical line at the average weight
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mtcars$wt), color = "blue") +
  # Add a title and axis labels
  labs(title = "geom_vline: average weight", x = "Weight", y = "mpg")
```

**Result:** one blue vertical line at x = 3.22 (the mean weight, in 1000 lbs).
